# 2 Samuel Chapter 20 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 192v–192r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_020_page_001.jpg, 2SA_020_page_002.jpg

---

**20:1** And-there happened [niqra'] to-be there a-man of-worthlessness [beliyya'al], and-his-name [was] Sheva son of-Bikhri, a-man of-Binyamin. And-he-blew on-the-shofar and-said, "There-is-no portion [cheleq] for-us in-David, and-no inheritance [nachalah] in-[the]-son of-Yishai. Each-man to-his-tents [le-ohalav], O-Yisra'el!"

**20:2** And-went-up every man of-Yisra'el from-after David, after Sheva son of-Bikhri. But-[the]-men of-Yehudah clung [davqu] to-their-king, from the-Yarden and-unto Yerushalayim.

**20:3** And-came David to his-house [in]-Yerushalayim, and-took the-king the-ten women, [the]-concubines [pilagshim] whom he-had-left to-keep the-house, and-put-them [in a]-house of-guarding [mishmeret]. And-he-provided-for-them, but to-them he-did-not go-in. And-they-were shut-up [atsurot] until [the]-day of-their-dying, [in]-widowhood of-living [almanut chayyut].

**20:4** And-said the-king to Amasa, "Call-to-me [the]-men of-Yehudah [within]-three days, and-you, stand here."

**20:5** And-went Amasa to-call Yehudah, and-he-delayed [vayyocher] beyond the-appointed-time [ha-mo'ed] that he-had-appointed-him [ye'ado].

**20:6** And-said David to Avishai, "Now he-will-do-worse [yera'] to-us Sheva son of-Bikhri than Avshalom. You take [the]-servants of-your-lord and-pursue after-him, lest he-find for-himself fortified cities [arey betsturot] and-tear-out [vehitstsil] our-eye [enenu]."

**20:7** And-went-out after-him [the]-men of-Yo'av, and-the-Kereti and-the-Peleti, and-all the-mighty-ones [gibborim]. And-they-went-out from-Yerushalayim to-pursue after Sheva son of-Bikhri.

**20:8** They [were] at the-great stone that [is] in-Giv'on, and-Amasa came before-them. And-Yo'av [was]-girded [with] his-garment [middo], his-clothing, and-upon-it [was] a-girding of-a-sword [chagor cherev] fastened upon-his-loins in-its-sheath [beta'arah]. And-he-went-out and-it-fell [vayyippol].

**20:9** And-said Yo'av to-Amasa, "Is-it-peace [ha-shalom] [with]-you, my-brother?" And-seized [the]-hand [of]-the-right of-Yo'av [the]-beard of-Amasa to-kiss-him.

**20:10** And-Amasa did-not guard [himself] against-the-sword that [was] in-[the]-hand of-Yo'av. And-he-struck-him [vayyakkeh-hu] with-it to the-belly [el-ha-chomesh], and-poured-out [vayyishpokh] his-inwards [me'av] to-the-ground, and-he-did-not repeat [it] to-him, and-he-died. And-Yo'av and-Avishai his-brother pursued after Sheva son of-Bikhri.

**20:11** And-a-man from-[the]-youths of-Yo'av stood over-him and-said, "Whoever delights [chaphets] in-Yo'av and-whoever [is]-for-David — after Yo'av!"

**20:12** And-Amasa [was]-rolling [mitgollel] in-the-blood in-[the]-middle of-the-highway [ha-mesillah]. And-saw the-man that all the-people stood-still, and-he-moved [vayyassev] Amasa from the-highway to the-field and-cast upon-him a-garment, when he-saw that everyone who-came upon-him stood-still.

**20:13** When he-was-removed from the-highway, every man passed-on after Yo'av, to-pursue after Sheva son of-Bikhri.

**20:14** And-he-passed through all [the]-tribes of-Yisra'el to-Avel and-Beyt-Ma'akhah and-all the-Berim, and-they-gathered and-came also after-him.

**20:15** And-they-came and-besieged him in-Avel of-Beyt-Ma'akhah, and-poured-out [vayyishpekhu] a-siege-mound [solelah] against the-city, and-it-stood against the-rampart [ha-chel]. And-all the-people who [were] with-Yo'av [were]-battering [mashchitim] to-bring-down the-wall.

**20:16** And-called a-wise [chakhamah] woman from the-city, "Hear, hear! Say, please, to Yo'av, 'Draw-near to-here, and-I-will-speak to-you.'"

**20:17** And-he-drew-near to-her, and-said the-woman, "Are-you Yo'av?" And-he-said, "I [am]." And-she-said to-him, "Hear [the]-words of-your-maidservant." And-he-said, "I [am]-hearing."

**20:18** And-she-spoke, saying, "Formerly [in the]-beginning they-spoke, saying, 'Asking let-them-ask [sha'ol yish'alu] in-Avel,' and-so they-settled [it] [vekhentammu].

**20:19** I [am one of the]-peaceable [shelumey] [and]-faithful [emuney] of-Yisra'el. You [are]-seeking to-kill a-city and-a-mother in-Yisra'el. Why will-you-swallow-up [tevalla'] [the]-inheritance [nachalat] of-YHWH?"

**20:20** And-answered Yo'av and-said, "Far-be-it [chalilah], far-be-it from-me, that I-should-swallow-up and-that I-should-destroy!

**20:21** Not so [is] the-matter. But a-man from-[the]-hill-country of-Ephrayim — Sheva son of-Bikhri [is] his-name — has-lifted his-hand against the-king, against David. Give-up him, him-alone, and-I-will-go from the-city." And-said the-woman to Yo'av, "Behold, his-head [shall be]-thrown [mushlakh] to-you over the-wall."

**20:22** And-came the-woman to all the-people in-her-wisdom [be-chokhmathah]. And-they-cut-off [vayyikhretu] [the]-head of-Sheva son of-Bikhri and-threw [it] to Yo'av. And-he-blew on-the-shofar, and-they-scattered [vayyaphutsu] from the-city, each-man to-his-tent [le-ohalav]. And-Yo'av returned to-Yerushalayim to the-king.

**20:23** And-Yo'av [was] over all the-army of-Yisra'el. And-Benayahu son of-Yehoyada [was] over the-Kereti and-over the-Peleti.

**20:24** And-Adoram [was] over the-forced-labor [ha-mas]. And-Yehoshaphat son of-Achilud [was] the-recorder [ha-mazkir].

**20:25** And-Sheva [was] scribe [sopher]. And-Tsadoq and-Evyatar [were] priests.

**20:26** And-also Ira the-Ya'iri was a-priest [kohen] to-David.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — beliyya'al:** The compound *beli-ya'al* means "without profit/worthlessness." Applied to Sheba, it marks him as a troublemaker in the deuteronomistic vocabulary. His rallying cry — "no portion in David" — echoes the language of tribal inheritance and will be repeated almost verbatim at the northern secession under Jeroboam (1 Kgs 12:16).

**v.3 — almanut chayyut:** "Widowhood of living" — an oxymoronic phrase describing the concubines' status: alive but treated as widows, permanently confined because Absalom had publicly violated them (16:22). This is one of the most troubling verses in the Davidic narrative.

**v.6 — vehitstsil enenu:** "And tear out our eye" — a difficult phrase. The verb *hitstsil* usually means "to deliver/rescue" (hiphil of נצל), but here it seems to mean "to snatch/tear away." Some read *enenu* as "our eye" (metaphor for something precious); others emend to "and escape us." The MT is preserved.

**v.8 — vayyippol:** "And it fell" — the subject is ambiguous. The sword fell from its sheath as Joab approached, placing it conveniently in his hand. This appears deliberate — Joab engineered the moment so the sword would seem to have fallen by accident.

**v.10 — el-ha-chomesh:** "To the belly" — the *chomesh* is the fifth rib area / abdomen. This is Joab's signature killing method: cf. Abner's death (2 Sam 3:27) and Asahel's (2:23). Joab consistently strikes to the belly, his lethal trademark.

**v.18 — sha'ol yish'alu be-Avel:** An infinitive absolute construction suggesting a proverbial saying: "They used to say in the old days, 'Let them inquire in Abel' — and so they settled matters." The wise woman invokes the city's reputation as a place of wisdom and arbitration.

**v.19 — shelumey emuney Yisra'el:** "The peaceable and faithful of Israel" — the woman identifies herself and her city with *shalom* (peace) and *emunah* (faithfulness/trustworthiness), positioning Abel Beth-maacah as a loyal Israelite city that should not be destroyed for one man's crime.

*— EMET*
